title: Tommy Dorsey's 'Marie' arrangement from a Black band; creativity ripped off
summary: Gil tells how Dorsey traded for a Black band's arrangement of 'Marie' and never paid them. He argues Black creativity was widely taken.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: No I don't indeed. I think 'I Can't Get Started With You' was the only big single he made wasn't it?

That arrangement, it reminds me of the arranging. Now Tommy Dorsey gave one of his arrangements to a band in Philadelphia that was sharing a stage show with him or something like that. A black band in Philadelphia played their arrangement of 'Marie' which was his arrangement that we know of so well. So Tommy said, 'oh I want that arrangement'. So they traded arrangements. You know they gave him one of his and they gave him one of theirs.

Well, of course he recorded it and being a, well being a merchant, he's going to, you've got to be chicken shit and greedy right? Because Chicken shit and greedy is built into world wide merchants, you can't help it, right? So, he of course, was not going to pay them any bonus or

anything like that. And I understand they did try to sue for him a little bit, because somebody told me recently, I forget who, but 'Marie' and 'Song of India' had been reissued on Victor 34 times the In different packages. And think of the money that Tommy Dorsey's estate made off that record 'Marie'.
The least he could do is send him like a little check for $50,000 or something in appeciation.
Of course I know so many stories like this now I've been interviewing black musicians for some years now.

That's the whole story right down the line. That's just a specific one. That's one that you could actually take and do something about it because it's got a name and a label and there it is and it's a sure example. But the whole tragic part of the thing is the general creativeness that went on was just generally ripped off, right?
That's what happened. Not the detailed single song for song for song thing. It was their whole feeling and the whole fire and life and
And that's not right, not to be able to perform. It's okay for somebody else to do what you do as long as you do what you do too, right? (LAUGHTER).
